title: US Immigration Data: open historical datasets on US immigration procedure and enforcement
description:
Machine-readable historical time series and reference datasets on United States immigration procedure and enforcement, maintained by MigrantUSA.

Why this exists: the underlying government sources publish the current value of most of this information and overwrite it without notice or archive. These datasets re-check those sources on a schedule and bank each observed change, so the history — what changed, when, and whom it affected — remains available in a form the official pages do not provide.

Contents: TPS designation, extension and termination history traced to Federal Register documents (1994–2026); USCIS filing-fee history across 40 forms with each change traced to its rule; month-over-month Visa Bulletin movement across all four tables; active 287(g) agreements with per-agency model and signing date; banked ICE detention statistics releases with computed change between releases; DOJ-recognized free legal-aid provision per immigration court; per-country TPS work-permit (EAD) status and current Form I-9 dates; and a verified dated change log.

Provenance: every value cites its official government source inside the file. The datasets are curation, normalization, verification and banked history over public government data; the underlying facts originate with the cited US agencies.

Formats: JSON is canonical and carries per-file metadata with source URLs and as-of dates; CSV flattenings are provided for convenience.
notes: Data collection is automated and runs daily; each dataset carries its own as-of date in its _meta block. The repository's CHANGES.md renders the recent change record in human-readable form.
